title: Editorial landing page
prompt: Design a long-form marketing landing page for "Fieldnote", a paid print-and-digital quarterly magazine about cities, architecture and the people who maintain them. Desktop, 1440px wide, full page (expect roughly 2400-3600px tall). The tone is editorial and confident, like a well-art-directed magazine, not a startup template. Sections in order: (1) top navigation with wordmark, links (Issues, Essays, Subscribe, About) and a Subscribe button; (2) a hero for Issue 14, "The Night Shift", with a large headline, a one-sentence dek, a cover or photographic image, and one primary call to action "Subscribe from $48/year"; (3) three featured essays with title, author, read time and an image each; (4) a pull quote from a contributor; (5) a subscription block comparing Digital ($24/year) and Print + Digital ($48/year) with what each includes; (6) a footer with newsletter signup and small print. Use real-feeling names and copy.
requiredContent: Nav links Issues, Essays, Subscribe, About and a Subscribe button
Hero for Issue 14 "The Night Shift" with headline, one-sentence dek and image
Three featured essays each with title, author, read time and image
Two plans: Digital $24/year and Print + Digital $48/year with inclusions

checklist.text: The six sections appear in the specified order (nav, hero, essays, pull quote, plans, footer).
"Subscribe from $48/year" is the single most visually prominent action above the fold (largest/most saturated button).
The hero headline is the largest text on the page and reads "The Night Shift" or clearly features it.
The hero uses a real photographic or illustrated image (not a gray box, broken image icon or empty placeholder).
Exactly three featured essays are shown, each with a title, author name, read time and an image.
The page uses at least two clearly distinct typefaces or a serif display face, giving an editorial rather than generic-SaaS voice.
Body text line length in essay teasers and dek is moderate (roughly 45-80 characters per line), not full-width.
The pull quote is typographically distinct (size, style or treatment) and attributed to a named person.
Both plans show prices $24/year and $48/year and list what is included; the recommended plan is visually distinguished.
Section spacing is consistent: vertical gaps between major sections look like one deliberate rhythm, not random.
No text is clipped, overlapping, or overflowing its container anywhere on the page.
No placeholder text or broken/missing images remain.
Footer contains a newsletter email field with a submit control.
Text over images remains legible (overlay, quiet area or contrast treatment), or text is not placed over busy imagery.
